title: How Much Does Tech Startup & Engineering Suite Janitorial Service Cost? Rates by Stage and Square Footage
seoTitle: Tech Startup Office Rates: Janitorial Cost Per Sq Ft & Per Month
metaDescription: Tech startup office rates for janitorial service run $0.07–$0.15 per sq ft per visit. Compare seed to Series B budgets, then price your suite in our tool.
excerpt: Tech startups pay $0.07 to $0.15 per sq ft per visit for most suites, but heavy kitchen use, open-plan density, and daily frequency drive monthly totals well above a quiet professional office. This guide benchmarks costs from seed-stage loft to Series B floor.
quickAnswer: A 3,000 sq ft seed-stage startup with polished concrete floors cleaned twice weekly typically pays $257–$428 per visit, or $2,221–$3,702 per month. An 8,000 sq ft Series A office on three-times-weekly service runs about $9,337–$15,561 per month, and kitchen-heavy teams should add $12–$25 per visit for breakroom sanitation.

blocks.text: Why Tech Startup Suites Price Differently From Traditional Offices

A startup office packs more people and more food into fewer square feet than almost any other office type. Benching layouts often run 100 to 150 sq ft per person versus 200 to 250 in a traditional office, kitchens are stocked with snacks and cold brew all day, and catered lunches several times a week produce compostable clamshells, sauce spills, and overflowing recycling. Add phone booths, a game area, a bike corner, and sometimes a shower room, and the crew spends far more time on waste and wet areas than on vacuuming.

The good news for budgets is flooring. Many engineering suites are in converted loft or flex buildings with polished concrete, which carries a 0.95 multiplier because an auto-scrubber or wide dust mop covers it quickly. The bad news is frequency: once headcount passes 25 to 30 people in a dense layout, weekly or twice-weekly service usually cannot keep the kitchen and restrooms acceptable, and daily service becomes the realistic standard.
Per-Sq-Ft and Monthly Benchmarks by Company Stage

The scenarios use national per-visit rates by size bracket, a flooring multiplier, and a frequency multiplier, with monthly totals calculated at 4.33 weeks per month. These cover base cleaning before breakroom, glass, consumables, and deep floor add-ons.

Two-person founder suite in coworking building

blocks.text: On a per-month basis the seed-stage loft works out to roughly $0.74 to $1.23 per sq ft, the Series A suite to $1.17 to $1.95, and the Series B floor to $1.30 to $2.22. The jump reflects frequency, not a higher hourly rate: daily visits multiply total labor even though the per-visit multiplier drops. For very small suites, the $90 to $135 per-visit minimum often sets the price.

blocks.title: Headcount is a better predictor than square footage
blocks.text: When two startups have the same square footage, the one with twice the headcount will generate roughly twice the kitchen waste and restroom use. Give every bidder your badge count and typical in-office days per week, not just a floor plan. Hybrid teams that are in office three days a week can often schedule full service on those days and a light trash and restroom pass on the others.
Restroom Density, Kitchens, and Traffic Wear

Startups in older loft buildings frequently have fewer restrooms than headcount requires, so each fixture room sees heavy use. Price restrooms at $15 to $30 per restroom per visit: three restrooms on the Series A three-times-weekly schedule add $585 to $1,170 per month (3 x $15 to $30 x 13 visits). Touchless foam soap dispensers such as the Rubbermaid AutoFoam 1100 mL unit, rated for up to 2,750 doses per refill with a roughly three-year battery, reduce mid-day outages and the number of high-touch surfaces crews must disinfect.

The kitchen is the single largest variable. Breakroom and kitchenette sanitation benchmarks at $12 to $25 per visit, which on daily service adds $260 to $541 per month. Teams with catered lunches, kegerators, or multiple espresso machines should expect the high end or a dedicated day porter. Traffic wear concentrates along the path from the elevator or entry to the kitchen and around desk clusters, where rolling chairs grind grit into carpet tiles or polished concrete.

Because engineers often work late, vacuuming must be quiet and cord-free. The ProTeam GoFree Flex Pro II backpack carries a 6 qt capacity with HEPA media and about 75 minutes of cordless runtime at roughly 18 lb with battery, suited to a full open-plan pass. For quick daytime spot work around desks, the Makita XCV17Z is a lighter 9.9 lb, 36V brushless backpack unit with a 2.0 L capacity and HEPA filter.
Recommended Weekly Frequency for Engineering Teams

items: Under 15 people with light snacks only: twice weekly full service, with founders handling kitchen wipe-downs between visits.
15 to 40 people, stocked kitchen, hybrid schedule: three times weekly aligned with in-office days, plus a light trash and restroom pass on remaining weekdays.
40 to 100 people with catered lunches: daily weekday service, breakroom sanitation every visit, and interior glass weekly.
100-plus people or 24/7 engineering on-call culture: daily service plus a day porter for 4 to 8 hours to reset kitchens, restock restrooms, and handle spills.
Hardware or robotics labs within the suite: separate lab scope with ESD-safe methods priced at specialty rates of $55 to $95 per hour.

blocks.text: Fully loaded, the Series A suite can reach $11,761 to $20,591 per month. Consumables are the line to scrutinize first: startups with an office operations lead can usually buy paper, soap, and liners more cheaply through a business purchasing account and have the vendor stock them.

faqs.q: How much does office cleaning cost for a small tech startup?
faqs.a: A 3,000 sq ft startup with polished concrete on twice-weekly service typically pays $0.09 to $0.15 per sq ft per visit times a 0.95 flooring multiplier, or about $257 to $428 per visit. That equals $2,221 to $3,702 per month at 8.66 visits, before restroom and kitchen add-ons.

faqs.q: Do startups really need daily cleaning?
faqs.a: Teams above roughly 40 people, or any team with catered lunches, usually do. Daily weekday service has a lower per-visit multiplier of 0.90, but 21.65 visits per month raises total cost. Hybrid teams can save by scheduling full service on in-office days and a light trash and restroom pass on the rest.

faqs.q: What insurance should a startup require from its cleaning vendor?
faqs.a: Request a certificate of insurance showing general liability of at least $1 million per occurrence, workers compensation, and a janitorial bond or third-party crime coverage, with your company and landlord named as additional insureds. Many landlords require this before granting after-hours access.

faqs.q: Can the cleaning crew wipe down keyboards and monitors?
faqs.a: Most scopes exclude electronics beyond exterior wipe-downs of shared devices with an approved electronics-safe product. Personal laptops, monitors, and engineering hardware should be explicitly excluded, and crews should never unplug equipment or touch server or IDF closets.

faqs.q: Is a day porter worth it for a growing startup?
faqs.a: Above about 100 people or with heavy kitchen use, a day porter for 4 to 8 hours often costs less than the productivity lost to empty soap dispensers and overflowing bins. Porters are typically billed at $35 to $65 per hour, the standard hourly benchmark.
